messages.content: if either cup is okay, does that mean i need both cups?
no. it says one cup or the other can work. you do not need both just because either is okay.
make a short request using that idea.
please bring me a cup. either of those two is okay.
what if only the blue one works?
then do not say either. say please bring the blue cup.
can either be useful when i do not want one more than the other?
yes. it says the other person can choose one of the two.
make that explanation shorter.
either leaves the choice between those two open.
only give the request with either again.
please bring me a cup. either of those two is okay.
write a longer story about a child saying a task is almost finished and another person asking what is left.

a child was making a picture for his sister. when she asked whether it was ready, he said it was almost finished. she began looking for a place to put it on the wall. he stopped her and explained that he still needed to draw the door and write one sentence under the house. she had heard almost as if it was ready now. they looked at the page together and chose to leave it on the table until those parts were done. later, when he said finished, he showed her the door and the line of writing. now she could put it up without having to bring it back for more work. saying what was left had helped more than the general word almost by itself.
was almost finished the same as ready to put on the wall?
not in this story. two parts still needed work.
what were those parts?
the door in the drawing and one sentence under the house.
can you know almost always gives two parts left?
no. almost is not a specific number of parts. the detail came from this story.
write a better answer from the child when asked if it is ready.
not yet. i still need to draw the door and write one sentence.
finish with the picture on the wall.
he finished the two parts and gave the page to his sister. together, they chose a place where both could see it.
use would rather in a sentence about choosing to read instead of watch a film.
i would rather read than watch a film.
does that mean i hate watching a film?
no. it says reading is the choice you want more in that moment. it does not have to be a rule for every day.
make that explanation shorter.
you can want reading now without saying a film is wrong.
now make a question asking my sister which she wants.
would you rather read or watch a film?
why or in the question and than in my answer?
or gives the two choices. than is the word used after would rather read in that answer.
make that explanation shorter.
use or to ask between choices, and than in the would rather answer.
only give the question again.
would you rather read or watch a film?
i keep a small list of words i want to use better. not many, just a few from things i read.
that gives you a place to return to the words instead of trying to remember all of them at once.
i like putting a sentence with each word. then it is not just a word by itself.
the sentence gives context for how you want to use it.
can you help me write a simple sentence with return?
i will return the book tomorrow.
now one where return is about going back to a place.
i will return home after lunch.
why can the same word be about a person or an object?
both have an idea of going or giving back. the sentence makes clear which one you mean.
make that explanation shorter.
return can be going back or giving something back.
only give the home sentence again.
i will return home after lunch.
write a longer story about someone asked to help with a book. they first think it is one page, then ask and learn it is a much longer task. keep the answer kind.

a woman was asked by her neighbor to help read a book. she thought he wanted help with one page and almost said yes right away. then she asked what kind of help he needed and how long it might take. he wanted someone to read the whole book with him over a few days. she did not have that much time. instead of giving a yes she could not keep, she said she could help with one page that evening but not the whole book. he said thank you for being clear and chose a page that was hard for him. they sat together long enough to understand that part. the smaller help was useful because they both knew what she could do and what she could not.
what did she first think the request was?
she thought he wanted help with one page.
what did she learn after asking?
he wanted help with the whole book over a few days.
make that answer more general without giving the number of days.
he wanted help over more than one day, and she said what part she could do.
why was the smaller yes better than a yes with no detail?
both knew the part she could help with. he did not have to plan around more time than she had.
make that explanation shorter.
he knew how much help to plan for.
finish with them ready to stop after that page.
when the page was clear, she said thank you for choosing one part. he put a note there so he could find it again.
what does i used to read here say?
it says reading here was something you did before. it often gives the idea that it is not what you do now.
make that explanation shorter.
you read here before, but often this sentence gives the idea you do not now.
can i still visit the place?
yes. the sentence is about reading here, not whether you can visit again.
now make a sentence about where i read these days.
i read at home now.
put the old and new reading places together.
i used to read here, but i read at home now.
only give that answer again.
i used to read here, but i read at home now.
can you know why i changed places?
no. you gave the change but not the reason.
write a longer story about two people talking about a visit and then understanding they mean different days. neither should be telling a lie.

a man asked his sister whether she had enjoyed the visit to their aunt. she said the meal had been quiet and only a few people were there. he remembered music and a full room. at first, they asked why what they remembered was so different. then she asked which day he was talking about. he was talking about the visit during the holiday, while she was talking about the small meal the week after. both had visited the same house and seen their aunt, but they were talking about different visits. once they gave the time, both stories could be understood together. they began again with the holiday visit first, then the smaller meal.
why did their first answers seem different?
they were talking about different visits without giving the day.
did that mean one had told a lie?
no. the story gives different days as the reason for the difference.
make that explanation shorter.
both answers could be true because the visits were not the same one.
what question made the difference clear?
which visit do you mean?
finish with a time added to the next question.
he asked about the holiday visit first. she answered about that day, and they could follow the same story together.
i can read, draw, or go for a walk. how many choices did i give?
three choices.
does that mean i will do all three?
no. giving three possible choices does not mean you have chosen all three.
make that answer shorter.
possible choices are not a plan to do everything.
now i say i will read and then walk. how many did i choose?
two: reading and walking.
can drawing still happen later?
it is possible, but you have not made it part of that plan.
only give the two things in order.
read, then walk.
what if the rain stops the walk?
then the plan changes. you can choose something else, but i should not choose it for you without knowing what you want.
i explained a sentence to my brother. i want to ask if it helped without making it sound like a test.
you could ask: was that clear, or would another example help?
can i ask what part he still wants to look at?
yes. which part would you like to look at again leaves room for a specific question.
what if he says it is clear?
then you can stop unless he asks for more. giving more examples is not always needed after the question is answered.
write a short reply to it is clear.
good. let me know if you want to look at another part later.
can you leave out later?
good. let me know if you want to look at another part.
only give the first question again.
was that clear, or would another example help?
can i say i had breakfast?
yes. i had breakfast is a simple sentence about eating breakfast before now.
now make it about my sister.
my sister had breakfast.
can i say she has had breakfast too?
yes. she has had breakfast can say breakfast is already done for her.
why is had in both?
had is used with breakfast in the sentence about the past. in has had breakfast, has goes before had to say the meal has already happened for her now.
make that explanation shorter.
she has had breakfast is useful when saying the meal is already done for her now.
can you know what she ate?
no. breakfast says which meal, not what food she ate.
make that explanation shorter.
breakfast does not give the food itself.
only give the first sister sentence again.
my sister had breakfast.
write a longer story about a child hearing yes without knowing the question. make it clear that yes alone is not enough information.

a child came into the kitchen just as his mother said yes to his brother. he thought that they were going outside, because he had been waiting for that answer before coming in. he began looking for his things. his mother asked why he was getting ready, and he told her what he had heard. she explained that his brother had asked for more water, not about going outside. yes had answered that question. the child sat down and asked whether they could go to the garden after lunch. this time, he knew which question the answer was for. hearing an answer had not given him the question that came before it.
what had the brother asked for?
more water.
why did the child think it was about going outside?
he had been waiting for an answer about that before he came in.
make that explanation shorter.
he heard yes and thought it was about his own plan.
what did he ask after the explanation?
whether they could go to the garden after lunch.
finish with the answer and its question clear.
his mother said yes to the garden after lunch. he said the plan back to check, then went back to his book until the meal.
i finished the book slowly. it took many days, but i kept coming back to it.
you stayed with it over time and got to the end. what made you want to return?
i liked the people, even when i could only read a little.
the people gave you a reason to keep reading in the time you had.
can you help me say that without making fast reading sound wrong?
i read the book slowly because i had little time, and i kept returning because i liked the people in it.
i did not say the reason was little time. sometimes i just wanted to read slowly.
i read the book slowly and kept returning because i liked the people in it.
can you add that sometimes i chose to read slowly, not that i always had little time?
sometimes i chose to read slowly, and i kept returning to the book because i liked the people in it.
does that say everyone should read slowly?
no. it gives how you read that book, not a rule for everyone.
there is a book and a cup on the table. i want my sister to bring only the book. give me a question.
could you bring me the book from the table, please?
what if i say could you bring it and she has not heard about either thing?
then it may not be clear what it is. saying the book is better when the other person does not have the context.
make that explanation shorter.
saying the book makes the choice clear if she does not know what it is about.
can i ask for both in one sentence?
could you bring me the book and cup from the table, please?
now ask for the cup instead of the book, only one thing.
could you bring me the cup from the table, please?
why did you leave out and?
you changed the request from two things to one. and was for asking about both.
only give the book question again.
could you bring me the book from the table, please?
i see three animals near a tree and two near the door. can you know what kind they are?
no. the word animals and their places do not give the specific kind.
how many animals did i say i see?
five, if those are different animals in the two places.
why did you add if?
one animal could be near both the tree and the door. if they are different animals in the two groups, there are five.
make that explanation shorter.
if one animal is in both groups, the number of different animals could be less than five.
explain when that could happen.
if the tree is near the door, one animal could be near both.
i mean two different groups now. only give the number.
five animals.
can you know they all eat the same food?
no. being animals does not tell us that all have the same food needs.
that is enough for now. do not tell me to do more.
okay. we can leave it there.
can you say something kind without saying i did everything right?
i hope the answer helps when you need it.
now only goodbye.
goodbye.
add take care, but nothing else.
goodbye, and take care.
the shop was open this morning. is it open now?
we do not know from that sentence. was open this morning gives a past time, not whether it is open now.
why can the answer for now be different from the morning?
the shop could have closed after the morning. a fact about one time does not always stay true at a later time.
just give the answer about now with no other detail.
we do not know whether the shop is open now.
now i say it is closed. put the old and new facts together.
the shop was open this morning, but it is closed now.
can both be true?
yes. the time changed, so the shop can have been open before and closed now.
only give the sentence with but again.
the shop was open this morning, but it is closed now.
